title: Expedition, classic, or *yacht-style*.
subtitle: Three different holidays that all get called a luxury cruise.

text: Style is the one mistake a good itinerary cannot rescue.
sub: You can change a suite, a date, even a route. You cannot change what a ship was designed to do with your evenings.

items.head: Expedition
items.body: Built around getting ashore in the boats: ice class, a lecture programme, naturalists. Dinner is early and unfussy.

items.head: Classic ocean
items.body: Larger, more venues, more structure. Strong for sea days, formal evenings and a proper library.

items.head: Yacht-style
items.body: Small, marina at the stern, dinner whenever. It reaches short quays, and the nights are the point.

points.label: First-timer
points.value: Yacht-style. Familiar rhythm, no fixed dining, and small enough to learn in a day.

points.label: Restless cruiser
points.value: Expedition. The novelty is the landings, and the ship stops being the entertainment.

points.label: Two weeks, one ocean
points.value: Classic. Sea days are designed for rather than endured, and the public rooms hold up.

points.label: Anyone for evenings
points.value: Yacht-style or classic. Expedition ships turn in early because the boats leave early.

text: Pick the style first. The itinerary is the easy part.
sub: Almost every disappointed traveller I have inherited did it the other way round — chose a route, then accepted whichever ship happened to be sailing it.

title: Send this to whoever you'd share a cabin with
body: Then tell me which of the three you think you are, and I'll tell you honestly whether I agree.
